Question B-008-004-007.

Why the correct answer is right: The affected TV channel range lines up with a harmonic of the amateur transmission, and other channels are not affected. That selective symptom points to harmonic emission.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "No high-pass filter on the TV": A missing high-pass filter on the TV would be a receiver-overload issue and would usually be less tied to only one harmonic-related channel.
- sourceIndex 2: "No high-pass filter at your transmitter": A high-pass filter at the transmitter would block the wanted HF output; transmitter output harmonic reduction uses low-pass filtering.
- sourceIndex 3: "Front-end overload of the TV": Front-end overload of the TV would tend to affect more than one harmonic-related channel and follow strong-signal level rather than a precise multiple.
